channel.title: RNZ New Zealand Headlines
channel.description: The Latest New Zealand headlines from RNZ News

item.title: Gisborne District Council unfairly criticised for forestry regulation handling - land use group
item.description: An independent review into the council's approach to the industry released this week found no evidence of anti-forestry bias.

item.title: The top 10 things to watch for in the US midterm elections
item.description: Analysis - There's more than one election this week. Here's what to watch for in America's pivotal midterms - and how they might affect New Zealand.

item.title: Political satire is having a renaissance during the 2026 election campaign
item.description: Not everyone is a fan, with Winston Peters calling one parody "just plain nasty".

item.title: Scrub fire under overbridge in Auckland's Eden Terrace investigated
item.description: The fire was underneath and alongside an overbridge, in a large area of trees and scrub.

item.title: Why are conservative KiwiSaver funds falling?
item.description: Morningstar data shows the peer group average for KiwiSaver conservative funds was a loss of 1 percent in the three months to September.

item.title: Desert wargames tax batteries, feed tech wishlist
item.description: The Defence Force has emerged from a series of high-tech experiments with the US army with a wishlist for more strike drones, more powerful batteries and more integrated robots, but also with a need to get the basics right - like more help with flights...

item.title: 15,000 borrowers struggling in hardship - latest data
item.description: The Centrix update shows "credit-active" consumers behind on their payments have increased to 10.88 percent.

item.title: 'Noticeable' spike in Dunedin car thieves targeting Subaru vehicles
item.description: Police say there is little or no sign of forced entry in many cases, and offenders are instead exploiting known vulnerabilities in some vehicle models.

item.title: 700 days with a catheter, seven months waiting for 'urgent priority' cancer care
item.description: David, who is 82, says he's repeatedly sought updates from Southland Hospital about his planned operation but has been met with unanswered emails and voicemail messages.

item.title: 'Most New Zealanders would be appalled': Abusive parents blocking children from therapy
item.description: A report by Backbone Collective details how abusive legal guardians are preventing their tamariki from accessing therapy and healthcare

item.title: Pharmac's cardiovascular team recommends funding Wegovy for some people
item.description: The drug is already in use in New Zealand, but unfunded, meaning patients must cover the cost.

item.title: Our Changing World: The tricky work of disentangling whales
item.description: Freeing whales trapped in fishing gear is dangerous work, but DOC teams train for it.

item.title: Household hot water savings 'could be bigger than solar'
item.description: Powerswitch head Paul Fuge says hot water controls have the potential to benefit households significantly, if they're used well.

item.title: Teaching Council under scrutiny as teacher charged with possessing objectionable material
item.description: Education Minister Erica Stanford is already critical of a "rotten culture" in the council, after other recent cases.

item.title: Hospital staff wait five months for agreed pay rise to kick in
item.description: The agreed 2.5 percent pay increase and $1000 lump sum won't reach workers' pockets until January next year, with Health NZ saying it has a backlog of collective agreements to implement.

item.title: Local iwi trust takes over troubled Pahīatua Medical Centre
item.description: Seven staff who recently resigned have been invited back under new management.

item.title: Review finds no evidence of anti-forestry bias at Gisborne District Council
item.description: The review was commissioned amidst criticism that the council was being "too tough" on forestry companies.

item.title: More mental health patients allowed community leave at time of murder - inquest
item.description: Laisa Waka Tunidau was stabbed to death by Zakariye Mohamed Hussein outside her Sockburn home in June 2022.

item.title: Millie Moon nappies told to investigate after complaints of rashes
item.description: MBIE has received five reports about Millie Moon nappies, with the complaints referring to a "rash/blisters forming" after using them.

item.title: Base jumper pleads guilty after getting stuck on side of Auckland hotel
item.description: He faced two charges of criminal nuisance.

item.title: Thousands of young people lose access to unemployment benefits
item.description: Unemployment rates are currently at an 11-year high.

item.title: Fires, rubbish and roaming dogs plague Gulf Harbour Country Club's fairways
item.description: In its heyday, the golf course was played on by Lydia Ko and hosted the World Cup of Golf and two New Zealand Opens.

item.title: Diwali celebrations bring colour, culture and a political jab to Auckland
item.description: Auckland's Diwali Festival brings together thousands to celebrate Indian culture while performers raise issues ranging from racism to politics on stage.

item.title: Home buyers warned about third-party LIM providers
item.description: Councils say some websites are offering LIMs for up to five times what the councils charge for a standard report.

item.title: 'Schooling was very much about assimilation' - Māori education leader honoured for work
item.description: Distinguished Professor Graham Hingangaroa Smith has spent his career advocating for Māori education systems.

item.title: 'Our people don't want handouts': Pasifika voters want action on bread-and-butter issues
item.description: Pasifika people in Aotearoa are saying this election is about the basics - getting kai on the table, petrol in the car, and access to affordable health services.

item.title: NZ minister opens Tongan detector dog facility to help fight illegal drug trade in Pacific
item.description: New Zealand has helped establish a new detector dog facility in Tonga, to curb the illegal drug trade around the Pacific.

item.title: Crown already has the man who killed Kyle Whorrall, says defence lawyer
item.description: One teenager has already pleaded guilty to Whorall’s murder, but four others are still on trial.

item.title: Missing Auckland man located days after backpack found in water
item.description: The 34-year-old man is safe, police say.

item.title: Nine arrested during 'unacceptable' Rugby League World Cup celebrations
item.description: South Auckland police were kept busy during a much-anticipated clash between Tonga and Samoa across the Tasman.

item.title: Fiji PM Rabuka delays vote on Constitution Bill after mounting pressure
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has given in to public pressure and made a complete U-turn from his position on tabling the controversial Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026 this week.

item.title: 'Markets so on edge for so long' - what KiwiSaver managers want you to know about AI fears
item.description: Investors are being advised to "stick to their knitting" and choose a fund that is right for them in the long term.

item.title: Victim 'incredibly shaken' after serious South Otago campground assault
item.description: More police can be expected around the Balclutha site over the next few days.

item.title: What does it take to build a sexy basket man?
item.description: Wētā Workshop's team of weavers, modellers and sculptors spent 18 months working out how to make Alexander Skarsgård the perfect wicker husband.

item.title: 'God's government': Samoan PM La'auli makes position clear on Israel
item.description: Prime Minister La'auli joined a pro-Israel parade in Apia over the weekend, where he broke down in tears, linking his support for Israel to his Christian faith.

item.title: Wellington trains resume after attempted cable theft causes delays
item.description: Police said the person was not apprehended and initial reports show no cables were damaged.

item.title: Man who died at Auckland beach identified
item.description: His body was spotted in the water at Saint Leonards Beach.

item.title: University of Canterbury researcher using laser beams to control tiny robots in hopes of medical breakthroughs
item.description: A researcher at the University of Canterbury studies micro-robots, about the size of one-hundredth of a human hair, to look at interactions between cells.

item.title: 'If not alive... repatriate my body': Family fears for woman stranded in Cook Islands
item.description: Ruchira Ranasingha, 50, fled Sri Lanka hoping to settle in Aotearoa but has been left stuck in limbo

item.title: Pahīatua Medical Centre, which suffered staff exodus sold to iwi
item.description: The decision follows months of turmoil at the medical centre with staff saying they were leaving over safety concerns.

item.title: Fijian PM Rabuka under pressure ahead of crucial vote on constitutional reform
item.description: Fiji's Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka's coalition government is falling apart ahead of the crucial third reading of a major bill to change the country's 2013 Constitution.

item.title: 'If not alive... repatriate my body': Family fears for Sri Lankan woman stranded in Cook Islands
item.description: The family of a Sri Lankan woman who has been stuck in the Cook Islands for three years because Australia and New Zealand refuses to let her transit warns her "mental state is not good".

item.title: Senior police staffer calls system for at-risk victims 'outdated'
item.description: It comes after the government shelved a system that would have supported "timely multi-agency responses" to family violence.

item.title: Which parts of NZ have shrinking population?
item.description: Some bigger cities have been losing people, and Wellington is back to the size it was in 2017.

item.title: Environmental breaches on dairy farms leading to bigger fines
item.description: Farmers can be fined up to a million dollars for serious environmental offending under tougher penalties introduced last year.

item.title: Why Tonga and Samoa can be the State of Origin of the new century
item.description: Analysis - It's not often you can feel when history is happening right around you but that is what happens when Samoa meets Tonga.

item.title: Husband of woman killed by bus calls for tougher driving tests for older drivers
item.description: Olawande Braimoh died after she was hit by a bus driven by a 72-year-old man who later admitted a charge of careless driving causing death.

item.title: Wellington school leavers want to stay, so why are they leaving the city?
item.description: A group of Year 13 students at Wellington High School told RNZ they feel like they have to leave the city they love to survive long-term.

item.title: Backroads to the Beehive: Fuel, food and the future at top of the south
item.description: Across the South Island, voters have singled out fuel, food and the future as the big issues on their mind at the ballot box and people at the top of the south are no different.
